extracted.intended_audience: Citizens of New York and the general public considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: A series of advocacy essays arguing for a single federal Union and the proposed Constitution, explaining practical political, commercial, fiscal, and defensive advantages of union versus disunion. Aimed to persuade public opinion and state ratifying conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union increases naval strength and national resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A national navy is more practicable and effective than any single State's or partial confederacy's navy because different States contribute complementary naval resources (tar, pitch, turpentine, durable wood, iron, and seamen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay explains that southern States supply naval stores and superior ship wood, some Middle and Southern States provide iron, and seamen must chiefly be drawn from the Northern hive. Combining these resources under one national government would improve ship durability, naval strength, and national economy compared to fragmented State navies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free intercourse between States advances trade and commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: Unrestrained intercourse among the States will advance each State's trade by allowing reciprocal supply of productions for domestic use and exportation to foreign markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free circulation replenishes 'veins of commerce' and increases motion and vigor. Diversity of production gives merchants broader scope, stabilizes trade when one staple fails, and makes foreign commerce more active and favorable due to variety and competition. The speculative trader will see aggregate commerce of the United States as more favorable than thirteen separate States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of government is necessary for unity of commercial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A unity of commercial interests can only follow from a unity of government; intimate intercourse under separate governments would be fettered, interrupted, and narrowed by multiple causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay anticipates the reply that intimate intercourse could persist despite disunion but argues that multiple obstacles (detailed elsewhere) would impair it, and only a single government can produce uniform, simple, and effective commercial regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union promotes national ascendancy and independence from European domination
rubrics_metrics.description: Union will enable the United States to achieve an ascendant position and vindicate national honor against European pretensions; disunion would invite foreign domination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author frames world politics as divided into parts dominated by Europe and argues that American union can resist European arrogance and influence. The moral imperative: Americans should 'disdain to be the instruments of European greatness' and erect one American system able to dictate terms with the Old World.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce is the principal source of national wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosperity of commerce is the most useful and productive source of national wealth; flourishing commerce multiplies gratification, introduces and circulates precious metals, and vivifies industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: commercial prosperity raises land value, promotes cultivation, increases money in circulation, and benefits all orders of men (merchants, husbandmen, mechanics, manufacturers). The essay criticizes the agriculture-versus-commerce rivalry and emphasizes their interdependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to pay taxes depends on money supply and circulation (commerce aids taxation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A country's ability to pay taxes correlates with the quantity of money in circulation and the speed of its circulation; commerce contributes to both and thus makes taxation easier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of commerce's role in increasing money supply and circulation, duties and indirect taxes become more productive. Examples contrast revenue-poor German hereditary dominions (despite mines and fertile land) with commercial nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: In America, revenue must rely chiefly on indirect taxes (duties and imposts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the difficulty of raising large sums by direct taxation in America, duties on imports and indirect taxes will be the principal means of revenue for the foreseeable future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excises are limited by public sentiment and the rural character of many States; taxes on land and personal property are problematic. Therefore, imposts and duties (indirect taxes) are the practical revenue sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: A single national government enables more effective collection of duties and reduces smuggling
rubrics_metrics.description: One government pervading all States allows guarding principally the Atlantic coast and simplifies detection and prevention of illicit trade, making duties far more productive than under separate States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under disunion, inland communications and proximity would facilitate contraband trade between States and with foreign countries; a few armed vessels at ports and coordinated measures under a national government would be sufficient and less expensive to prevent infractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union allows higher, more productive rates of duties without harming trade
rubrics_metrics.description: With effective national enforcement, duties can be raised substantially (potentially tripling current State averages) without prejudice to trade, yielding significant revenue (example: ardent spirits duty estimation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States' current duties average around three percent; in France and Britain they are higher. The essay gives a concrete example: a shilling per gallon on spirits could produce substantial revenue and have beneficial social effects by reducing consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: A nation without adequate revenue loses independence
rubrics_metrics.description: A country cannot long exist without revenues; lacking them, it will resign independence and become a province — therefore revenue must be secured by feasible means at all events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If commerce cannot furnish revenue (because of disunion), the burden will fall oppressively on landowners. Thus, practical revenue considerations argue strongly for union to open all revenue sources to the national government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union yields economy in government through consolidation of civil lists and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: A single national government reduces duplication: there will be one civil list and fewer comprehensive institutions than if the States were divided into confederacies, producing savings that can be applied elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If divided into confederacies, each would require principal departments coextensive with those necessary for a government of the whole; population and territory comparable to Britain imply similar administrative needs, so multiple governments mean multiplied expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disunion increases costs for patrols, military establishments, and inland enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate confederacies would require many persons to guard inland communications against illicit trade and large military establishments due to jealousies and conflicts, eroding economy and tranquility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay cites France's extensive patrols against contraband as an example of the high cost and arbitrary power required to enforce fiscal regulations when many internal frontiers exist, an intolerable burden in a free country.

rubrics_metrics.name: A republic (by representation) can govern an extended territory — representation distinguishes republic from democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The practical limit of a republic is set by the ability of representatives to meet, not by the ability of the people to assemble in person; thus an extended republic is practicable, unlike a pure democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distinction explains why fears that republican government must be confined to a small territory are fallacious. Historical confounding of 'republic' with 'democracy' and examples (Britain, German diet, Poland) support the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal government should be limited to enumerated national objects; states retain other authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The general government's jurisdiction is confined to specifically enumerated matters that concern all members of the republic; subordinate state governments remain active over local subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This federal arrangement mitigates concerns about governing a large territory because local matters remain with states, while the national government handles common needs; abolishing state governments would raise different issues but is not proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements in communication and infrastructure will make governance and intercourse easier
rubrics_metrics.description: Roads, better accommodations for travelers, interior navigation, and canals will shorten and facilitate communication across the Union, increasing practicability of a large republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay anticipates progressive improvements connecting Western and Atlantic districts and easing travel for representatives and citizens, reducing objections based on distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distant or frontier States derive compensating benefits from Union (defense and resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: States far from the seat of government may reap less ordinary circulation benefits but will gain more from national defense and resources due to proximity to foreign nations; this maintains equilibrium of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if travel to the seat of government is inconvenient, frontier states would prefer the shared strength and expense of the Union rather than struggling alone against invasion or bearing disproportionate defense costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing practice shows representation over distance is feasible (empirical practicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that representatives from distant States have long attended Congress indicates that the distances within the United States do not exceed practicable limits for a representative government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative distances (Atlantic to Mississippi, degrees of latitude) and historical experience (thirteen years of representatives assembling) are used to argue empirically for practicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: The present Confederation is insufficient to preserve the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: The existing national system contains material imperfections and cannot secure stable union and safety; something more effective (the proposed Constitution) is necessary to prevent impending anarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay frames this as commonly admitted by both proponents and opponents of the new Constitution and sets the stage for further argument and factual illustrations demonstrating the Confederation's insufficiency.
